So, we urging our citizens that those are things being agreed upon by the partner's state" ; "We have to make sure that we respect those laws because when you are visiting any or one of these partners' states who are members of East African communities you must make sure that if your three months are expired you need to visit the nearest immigration office and they will renew your three months' free visa."

a4722.speaker: South Sudan Embassy in Kenya (notice)
a4722.speech: Issued a notice advising citizens of the new visa fees, which require South Sudanese nationals to pay $201 for a six-month overstaying extension, and stated that extensions for travel documents or passports will cost $51 if not renewed.

a4722.speaker: Kenya Foreign National Service
a4722.speech: Announced a penalty of $601 for individuals overstaying beyond six months, and stated individuals seeking extensions of their travel documents will pay fifty-one dollars ($51).

a4722.speaker: William Ruto, President of Kenya
a4722.speech: Announced early this year that foreign tourists would no longer be required to pay visas.

a4772.speaker: Berhan Bank (BB) financial statement
a4772.speech: The financial statement indicated that the interest income has expanded by 60.5 percent compared with a similar period a year ago, reaching 1.1 billion birr.

a4772.speaker: Berhan Bank (BB)
a4772.speech: BB claimed that their profits had gone down somewhat because of the country's socio-economic situation which has put pressure on the entire banking industry.

a4772.speaker: Berhan Bank (BB) statement / annual report
a4772.speech: According to BB's statement, in the 2017/18 financial year the bank earned 410 million birr profit before tax, a slight decrease from last period's 428 million birr; according to the annual report the earnings per share was 20.4 percent, which means it was 30 percent per 1,000 birr share; and the bank's total capital has reached 2.2 billion birr with a paid up capital of 1.7 billion birr, an increase of 22.4 percent.

a5023.speaker: US State Department
a5023.speech: Has issued instructions to the agencies implementing PEPFAR (President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief) to resume HIV services immediately, despite the 90 day “pause” in US aid.

a5023.speaker: Mozambican parliament’s HIV/AIDS Prevention Office
a5023.speech: Says this is a “limited exemption”, for the sole purpose of saving lives, under which HIV treatment services can be resumed, including counselling, HIV testing, preventing and treating opportunist infections (including tuberculosis), laboratory services, and management of the medical supply chain ; says the exemption also covers the prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV, including pre-exposure prophylaxis for pregnant and lactating women, and that PEPFAR funds can be used for “reasonable administrative costs necessary for delivering the assistance” ; says it covers tests of the HIV viral loads “which allow monitoring of the patient to guarantee that the medicines for treating HIV are effective”, and that the treatment of tuberculosis is covered because “TB is the greatest cause of death among people living with HIV” ; says the “limited exemption” does not cover “activities that involve abortion or family planning”, or “gender ideology programmes, transgender surgery, or other activities that do not save lives”.

a5023.speaker: Mozambican parliament’s HIV/AIDS Prevention Office
a5023.speech: Argues that these results “reflect the positive impact of consistent public policies, of expanding the coverage of the health services, and of mobilising national and international resources”.

a5023.speaker: National AIDS Council (CNCS) of Mozambique
a5023.speech: Latest statistics provided by the CNCS show that 12.5 per cent of adults over 15 years of age are HIV-positive, with prevalence higher among women (15 per cent) than men of the same age, the most affected group being girls and young women aged between 15 and 24, among whom 23,000 new infections were registered in 2023 ; the CNCS believes that, over the past two decades, 1.7 million new HIV infections and 1.1 million HIV-related deaths have been avoided.

a5061.speaker: Dr. Abebe Genetu Bayih, Acting Lead, Platform for Harmonized African Health Products Manufacturing (PHAHM), Africa CDC
a5061.speech: “We see promising developments on the continent and we're looking at engaging with all the stakeholders to join forces with Africa CDC as we strive to achieve the AU's ambition to manufacture 60% of vaccines needed by 2040,” told The Independent in an email interview.

a5061.speaker: Prof. Pontiano Kaleebu, Director of the Uganda Virus Research Institute (UVRI)
a5061.speech: “We need to build capacity, attract good scientists, attract funding, encourage tech transfer, work with Africa CDC and many others, including the World Health Organization (WHO), and the whole international community.”

a5061.speaker: Rangarirai Machemedze, Coordinator of the Zimbabwean chapter of the Southern and Eastern Africa Trade Information and Negotiations Institute (SEATINI)
a5061.speech: Said that, in Africa, operational costs are often high because of very old (pharmaceutical) plants, skilled workers cannot be retained, tariffs on water and electricity are high, and working capital and technology are often lacking.

a5061.speaker: Nazeem Mohamed, international pharmaceutical consultant
a5061.speech: Told delegates that besides African pharmaceutical manufacturers requiring huge sums of capital to set up vaccine plants capable of producing 15 legacy vaccines, they would also need partnerships with bigger pharmaceutical industries in the West to share technology ; “That will not come cheaply.”

a5061.speaker: Africa CDC Partnerships for African Vaccine Manufacturing (PAVM) strategy (document)
a5061.speech: Highlights the need for stakeholders, including private sector actors, to support its vision, build sufficient human capital and skills, and raise finance for the vaccine manufacturing value chain on the continent.

a5061.speaker: Natasha Kofoworola Quist, communications specialist at VaxSen, the commercial subsidiary of Institut Pasteur de Dakar
a5061.speech: Says the MADIBA project, named after Nelson Mandela, embodies the spirit of African self-reliance and innovation and is focused on developing and scaling up the production of affordable, high-quality vaccines for diseases that disproportionately affect Africa, such as yellow fever, measles, and COVID-19, by leveraging cutting-edge mRNA and other advanced vaccine production technologies ; “It involves collaborations with global stakeholders, including governments, multilateral organisations, and private sector partners, to share knowledge, resources, and expertise.”

a5061.speaker: Javier Niño Pérez, European Union Ambassador to the African Union
a5061.speech: Says that by the end of 2024, MAV+ had mobilized investments in excess of €2 billion through 99 projects funded in a coordinated “Team Europe” approach by the European Union, EU member states Belgium, Germany and France, the European Investment Bank, and European Development Financing Institutions ; says the EU is also enhancing integration of African health product markets with €750 million to the African Vaccine Manufacturing Accelerator (AVMA), which is expected to purchase more than 800 million doses produced in Africa over the next decade.

a5061.speaker: Javier Niño Pérez, European Union Ambassador to the African Union
a5061.speech: Also told The Independent that one effective modality of working with the AU across the work streams are the “embedded experts” who are working at Africa CDC and the AUDA-NEPAD, funded by Team Europe.

a5061.speaker: Experts who spoke to The Independent (unnamed)
a5061.speech: Remain guarded, saying achieving the objective of expanding end-to-end African vaccine manufacturing capacity will require a carefully structured “Advance Market Commitment” that right-sizes volume targets and payments, which is what will incentivise manufacturer entry without creating barriers to future entrants or compromising market stability ; have also told The Independent that market shaping strategies and affordable financing should be complemented with building human skills and capacities and sharing of crucial knowledge around vaccine technologies and intellectual property: “This applies not just to manufacturing but also to the full vaccine value chain, from research capacity and laboratory networks through to the manufacture of ancillary supplies, and which will require considerable and broad-based investment.”

a5061.speaker: Recent modelling (study cited)
a5061.speech: According to recent modelling, the importation of skilled workers is a major potential cost driver for new vaccine manufacturing facilities in Africa.

a5061.speaker: Dr. Jean Kaseya, Director General of Africa CDC
a5061.speech: “Between 9000 and 14,000 full time employees will be needed in vaccine manufacturing and research roles across Africa by 2040.”

a5061.speaker: Manuel Batz, Lead for the Global Programme BACKUP Health at the German International Development Agency (GIZ)
a5061.speech: Told The Independent that regional collaboration is important, and the establishment of Regional Capability and Capacity Networks (RCCNs) is a key step forward; says that by working as a network, RCCNs can ensure that knowledge is shared and that the right skills are built at the right scale, and that skill and talent development is all about combining education, training, and collaboration – both locally and internationally.

a5061.speaker: Manuel Batz, Lead for the Global Programme BACKUP Health at the German International Development Agency (GIZ)
a5061.speech: On technology transfer: “With the right legal frameworks and support, both parties can find a way to make this work for Africa's vaccine manufacturing ambitions”; says the Medicines Patent Pool (MPP) negotiates voluntary licensing agreements and enables technology transfers, a good example being the mRNA Technology Transfer Programme, which BACKUP Health supports ; “It's about creating win-win partnerships – where Africa gets the support it needs to build manufacturing capacity and international companies see the long-term value in being part of the solution.”

a5061.speaker: Berlin Declaration, International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers & Associations (IFPMA)
a5061.speech: Showed industry intent to accelerate manufacturing partnerships, business-to-business agreements, capability development support, voluntary licensing and/or early, voluntary technology transfer.

a5061.speaker: Dr Mimi Darko, Chief Executive Officer, Ghana Food and Drugs Authority
a5061.speech: “It is fulfilling to see the commitment that the Heads of African NRAs have towards collaborating with a common goal of ensuring timely access to safe, quality and effective medical products in Africa.” ; “As we sign this MoU, we — the ML3 NRAs on the continent — commit ourselves to leading efforts toward a more harmonised regulatory landscape that strengthens local manufacturing and improves access.”

a5098.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a5098.speech: “I’m pleased to share that we have completed and ceased the military operations in the Tigray region,” said Prime Minister Abiy, using the same social media platform where 26 days ago he announced the launching of military operations there ; According to Prime Minister Abiy, the Defense Forces are in control of the Northern Command Camp, the airport, public institutions, and the regional administration office.

a5098.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a5098.speech: Prior to launching the latest military offensive, he had issued a 72-hour ultimatum to the regional forces to surrender or face a military offensive in the state’s capital of Meqelle, and set out three goals to the military operation he ordered on November 3, 2020: Disarming the TPLF, bringing its leaders to trial, and installing a provisional administration until elections are held in the Regional State.

a5098.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a5098.speech: What lies ahead is rebuilding the damaged infrastructure in the Regional State, while returning and rehabilitating the tens of thousands of refugees back to their homes will be top priorities, according to the Prime Minister. "Our focus now will be on rebuilding the region and providing humanitarian assistance while Federal Police apprehend the TPLF clique," Prime Minister Abiy tweeted on Saturday.

a5098.speaker: Birhanu Jula (Gen.), Army Chief of Staff
a5098.speech: Aired by state broadcaster Ethiopian Broadcast Corporation (EBC), Chief of Staff Birhanu said no casualties occurred to residents of Meqelle during the operation, and residents remained in their homes when the Defense Forces took over the city ; The Army has also liberated over 7,000 members of the Northern Command that were held hostage by the TPLF, according to Berhanu, who said that the Defence Forces are now in complete control of Meqelle and “fully controlled” the city. "The people of Tigray should be the most overjoyed at this victory."

a5098.speaker: Redwan Hussein, spokesperson of the state of emergency secretariat
a5098.speech: Announced that ''essential parts'' of Meqelle, such as the airport and “several locations” have fallen under the control of the Defense Forces.

a5098.speaker: World leaders
a5098.speech: Urged Ethiopia’s leaders to show restraint and caution when conducting the final military assault on the city to safeguard the civilian population estimated at over half a million.

a5098.speaker: Ethiopian Human Rights Commission and Amnesty International
a5098.speech: Disclosed a mass killing of over 600 people in Mai-Kadra, a town in the South-West Zone of Tigray Regional State.

a5098.speaker: Leaders of both sides (federal government and Tigray regional government)
a5098.speech: Blame one another for these atrocities.

a5098.speaker: Sources (anonymous)
a5098.speech: It appears that there was no fighting in the city, after a possible withdrawal of TPLF political and military leaders and its forces from the city, according to sources.

a5098.speaker: Officials from the federal government
a5098.speech: Officials from the federal government were not available for comment.

a5098.speaker: United States Institute for Peace (report)
a5098.speech: A recent report warns that while the fighting of the last few weeks may have significantly degraded the TPLF’s military capacity, it is unlikely that the federal government can entirely subdue the TPLF as a political entity. ”The TPLF’s historic capacity to wage guerrilla warfare from the rural mountains of Tigray may not be definitively eroded by its losses in conventional warfare,” says the report.

a5098.speaker: Gedion Timothewos (PhD), Attorney General / Office of the Attorney General
a5098.speech: Announced that 167 individuals are suspected of alleged crimes linked to the incident in Tigray Regional State and are to face criminal charges including high treason, armed rebellion, outrage against the Constitution, acts of terrorism related to firing rockets and hostile acts against a friendly country.

a5248.speaker: Yoboua Koffi, director of project planning and financing at Sodefor
a5248.speech: "During these four months, we arranged for them to spend 45 days at Maitre Jardin. They did theoretical and practical training. They are now able to set up on their own account. They did three months of training at Anguededou, then at Yamoussoukro with the gardeners and at Oume within Sodefor" ; according to him, this support reflects his organisation's desire to back the government in its youth insertion policy, and he expressed his gratitude to Maitre Jardin, which handled the training, as well as to the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC), an American foreign aid agency, the initiative being a gift from the United States to Cote d'Ivoire.

a5248.speaker: Jacques Nader, manager of Maitre Jardin
a5248.speech: Recounted the history of the training; according to him, it allowed these young people to learn trades that will make them the men of tomorrow.

a5248.speaker: Nabi Ibrahim Danko, graduate trained in biological sciences (forestry option), speaking on behalf of the recipients
a5248.speech: Thanked Maitre Jardin, the MCC, the MCE (Maison des chefs d'entreprise) and Sodefor, who enabled them to strengthen their skills: "We learned layering, grafting and the names of the different plants that we did not know. It is a new experience and an opportunity offered to us. They will allow us to take up this profession."

a5255.speaker: Economists (collectively, in Tanzania)
a5255.speech: Have praised the rising dividends and contributions from State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) as a crucial step toward Tanzania's financial self-reliance, saying that the trend will significantly strengthen the government's capacity to fund the national budget using domestic resources and reduce dependency on external borrowing.

a5255.speaker: Dr Hildebrand Shayo, economist and investment banker
a5255.speech: Described the surge in SOE dividends as a significant milestone with positive economic and fiscal implications, especially as Tanzania works to rely more on internal resources; noted that this upward trend may be reflected in the budget to be presented to Parliament today, showcasing how President Samia Suluhu Hassan's administration is prioritising domestic revenue mobilisation ; "The collections that have increased this financial year (261bn/-) will enable the government to fund its priorities without turning to loans or external aid" ; added that the increasing SOE contributions will help reduce the budget deficit, finance essential public services such as education, health and water, and gradually minimise the country's dependence on foreign aid and debt ; "This initiative aligns with the goals outlined in Vision 2025 and the Third National Five-Year Development Plan (FYDP III)" ; said a robust domestic revenue base will help Tanzania avoid costly commercial borrowing and exposure to foreign exchange volatility, while also easing the tax burden on citizens ; noted that improved macroeconomic indicators are likely to attract foreign investment and enhance Tanzania's credit rating, and argued that continued reforms, modernisation and adequate funding for SOEs could unlock even greater returns ; "If government expenditure from SOE dividends is channeled into infrastructure, job creation and private sector development, the ripple effects will drive GDP growth and contribute to poverty reduction" ; cautioned that attention must be given to the long-term sustainability of SOE contributions: "A 68 per cent increase in dividends is a commendable milestone, but we must ensure good governance and efficiency in SOEs operations to maintain this momentum."

a5255.speaker: Professor Kitojo Wetengere, University of Arusha (UoA)
a5255.speech: Commended the high performing SOEs for supporting the government's domestic revenue agenda; noted that institutions like the Tanzania Ports Authority (TPA), which topped this year's list with 181.5bn/-, up from 153bn/- last year, are reducing their reliance on central government funding, unlike struggling SOEs that remain financially dependent ; urged the government to appoint competent directors with strong academic and practical backgrounds to lead SOEs and boost efficiency ; advocated for privatisation of non-performing public entities to improve service delivery and sustainability.

a5394.speaker: United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) (statement)
a5394.speech: estimated on Thursday that around 4.8 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance in Mozambique, with US$64 million required to “address the humanitarian needs of 2.5 million people nationwide, including 2.1 million children” ; “The poly-crisis in Mozambique – conflict, drought and public health emergencies – are stretching humanitarian resources. Approximately 4.8 million people require humanitarian assistance (10% of these, persons with disabilities), including 3.4 million children” ; on Cabo Delgado, explains that “more than 1.3 million internally displaced people, returnees and conflict-affected people require assistance”, adding that “80% of returnees and those who are internally displaced are women and children” ; “Nearly 3.3 million people are projected to be in ‘crisis’ or higher levels of food insecurity due to the impact of the El Niño weather pattern, while La Niña weather patterns may exacerbate conditions in 2025” ; “more than 29,000 children under age 5 will likely need treatment for severe wasting (acute malnutrition)” ; “A lack of predictable and flexible funding puts children’s welfare at risk.”

a5394.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a5394.speech: In September, the United Nations reported that almost two million people in Mozambique were in need of humanitarian assistance: “Due to the impact of the drought induced by the El Niño phenomenon during the 2023-2024 season, the humanitarian assistance needs of affected communities have increased substantially, particularly in the Central and Southern Regions of Mozambique. It is expected that approximately 1.8 million people may experience food insecurity between October 2024 and March 2025.”

a5486.speaker: Joel Gamys, Executive Director of the Forestry Training Institute (FTI)
a5486.speech: Says the move is a significant step toward improving educational facilities; expresses gratitude to government for facilitating the project, which is the first civil work undertaken by the institution ; "This is a moment of transformation for FTI, and it is the result of teamwork among the institution's administration. We aspire to make FTI a leading institution in the country" ; emphasizes that the renovation aligns with President Boakai's ARREST AGENDA, underscoring their commitment to overcoming challenges rather than being overwhelmed by them; expresses optimism about the institution's trajectory, believing the improvements will yield substantial benefits for future students.

a5486.speaker: Joel Gamys, Executive Director of the Forestry Training Institute (FTI)
a5486.speech: Points out that ongoing support from the Liberian government is crucial for the institution to achieve its objectives; commended government for its unwavering support towards the institution.

a5486.speaker: Joel Gamys, Executive Director of the Forestry Training Institute (FTI)
a5486.speech: Reveals that the Commission on Higher Education recently accredited the FTI, elevating its programs from diploma level to Associate Degree.

a5486.speaker: Ezekiel Dolo, Project Officer
a5486.speech: Details scope of the renovations, which include residential buildings, cafeteria, health course facilities, and kitchen; says the project, initially constructed by the Mano River Union, suffered destruction during the country's civil war ; "This is the first significant infrastructure development project undertaken by the government since it assumed office, aimed at revitalizing FTI and enhancing its facilities."

a5670.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Tanzanian Vice President
a5670.speech: Has hailed Tanzania’s first female President, Dr. Samia Suluhu Hassan, for her role in implementing policies and actions that strengthen the position of women in all sectors of society regionally, while internationally she has been an advocate for peace, justice, security, and the use of clean energy; speaking while addressing the 80th Session of the United Nations General Assembly, he called for the full participation of women in the pursuit of peace, especially during this period, 30 years since the Beijing Declaration.

a5670.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Tanzanian Vice President
a5670.speech: Said that Tanzania joins other countries in demanding urgent and comprehensive reforms of the international financial system: “I call for increased long-term concessional financing, reform of independent credit rating systems, and a rethink of debt sustainability assessments, to secure capital for investments in infrastructure, education, health, and climate change resilience” ; stressed the desire to increase Africa’s voice and representation in the governance structures of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank, which has not been done for a long time.

a5670.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Tanzanian Vice President
a5670.speech: Said Tanzania is committed and has made progress in implementing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 2030, reaching 60 percent; said that for goal number 3, Tanzania has succeeded in reducing maternal mortality from 750 deaths per 1000 live births in 2000 to 104 in 2022 ; “For goal number 6, access to clean and safe water increased in rural and urban areas from 32 percent and 55 percent in 2000 to 79.9 percent and 94 in 2024. With affordable clean energy, which is goal number 7, Tanzania has successfully connected electricity to 8,587 villages in (2000) to 12,318 in 2024 where only 15 villages remain without electricity.”

a5670.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Tanzanian Vice President
a5670.speech: Urged the international community to strengthen a collective response to climate change, including a call to make good use of the opportunity of the COP30 Conference in Brazil to ensure that commitments are implemented including contributions to the Fund for Losses and Disasters due to the effects of climate change: “This includes increasing long-term concessional financing, technology transfer, and fair trade conditions to achieve domestic revenue collection for countries and seek mutually beneficial cooperation in the use of resources.”

a6004.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of the United Republic of Tanzania, and Duma Gideon Boko, President of the Republic of Botswana (joint op-ed)
a6004.speech: Write that the challenge of malaria is also caused by reduced funding from major donors, including the recent cuts to United States foreign aid, which historically has been the leading supporter of malaria elimination through the President's Malaria Initiative (PMI) and the Global Fund; the suspension of USAID funding has set back efforts to fight malaria through the decline in essential malaria commodities in many countries, especially in Africa.

a6004.speaker: Experts (cited estimate)
a6004.speech: Estimate that if aid funds continue to be unavailable, Africa will see an additional 112 million cases and 280,000 malaria deaths between 2027 and 2029, and that reduced Global Fund financing will push cases to 137 million and deaths to 337,000, reversing the gains of past decades.

a6004.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of the United Republic of Tanzania, and Duma Gideon Boko, President of the Republic of Botswana (joint op-ed)
a6004.speech: Argue that without swift corrective action the challenge will grow, endangering more children's lives and creating obstacles for health, the economy and regional stability; that Africa needs an additional USD 5.2 billion each year to fully implement national malaria control strategies; and that eliminating malaria requires strong momentum on all fronts - sustained availability of prevention, diagnosis and treatment, data-driven decisions, international cooperation, and mobilisation of domestic resources.

a6004.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of the United Republic of Tanzania, and Duma Gideon Boko, President of the Republic of Botswana (joint op-ed)
a6004.speech: "As Presidents of Tanzania and Botswana, we affirm our shared commitment to ending the disease of malaria, not only in our countries, but across the whole of Africa." ; state that this momentum begins with closing the funding gap, that international funding is essential and financial support from the Global Fund must be secured, and that Tanzania and Botswana are ready to lead that momentum and invite others in Africa and around the world to join them.

a6004.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of the United Republic of Tanzania, and Duma Gideon Boko, President of the Republic of Botswana (joint op-ed)
a6004.speech: Note that less than 2 percent of malaria commodities are manufactured in Africa, that increasing local production is no longer optional but essential, and that Africa must move from being the world's largest consumer to being a major producer.

a6075.speaker: Walde Ndevashiya, Governor of the Ohangwena Region (Namibia)
a6075.speech: Said all men should go and get circumcised, because it is important for a person to be circumcised in order to preserve his health ; said that when a person is circumcised he has a lower chance of being infected with HIV and also protects his partner in a sexual relationship from contracting various diseases ; “Now this is a good opportunity for all the men of Ohangwena to make use of this clinic so that they take care of their health, because when a man is circumcised he has a 60% chance of not being infected with the virus” ; advised parents to bring their young boys while they are still small so that they are circumcised, because it is important for a child to be circumcised at a young age ; added that people should share information about the importance of circumcision so that men and children are encouraged to take an interest in being circumcised.

a6075.speaker: Walde Ndevashiya, Governor of the Ohangwena Region (Namibia)
a6075.speech: Said he thanked the USAID organisation for having built the clinic that will be used to circumcise men, and said the clinic was built with the aim of providing medical services to men so that they will come forward to be circumcised.

a6075.speaker: Daniel Lee, representative of USAID
a6075.speech: Said in his speech that they aim to support the government through preserving the health of men ; said the aim of the clinic is to change the situation of men so that they are protected from various diseases, because it helps them when they are circumcised ; added that the ministry of health should continue to provide information to the public so that men have sufficient understanding of how important it is for a person to be circumcised.

a6146.speaker: African Union Peace & Security Council (PSC)
a6146.speech: In a recent session dedicated to updating the political transitions in these countries, the PSC stressed several concerns. Chief among them is the deteriorating security situation in the Sahel region, fueled by terrorist and insurgent groups and leading to dire humanitarian conditions ; The PSC urged the AU Commission, the international community, and capable member states to provide humanitarian assistance.

a6146.speaker: Moussa M. Faki, AU Commission Chairperson
a6146.speech: Acknowledged the lack of meaningful intervention during an address to the AU Assembly in February this year. He posed rhetorical questions that spotlighted the gravity of the situation and the AU's inadequate response.

a6146.speaker: African Union Peace & Security Council (PSC)
a6146.speech: In the case of Niger, the PSC tasked the AU Commission to swiftly deploy a high-level mediation mission to engage with transitional authorities and establish a transition roadmap aligned with national and regional dispositions.

a6146.speaker: African Union Peace & Security Council (PSC)
a6146.speech: Concerning Mali, it requested the Commission to urgently organise a fact-finding mission to discuss the conclusions of the inter-Malian dialogue and collaborate with transitional authorities to identify opportunities for cooperation and implementation.

a6146.speaker: African Union Peace & Security Council (PSC)
a6146.speech: For Gabon, the PSC noted the setting of the transition duration for two years, with intentions to hold elections in August 2025. It expressed rejection of any further extension and renewed its call for a speedy return to constitutional order within the prescribed timeframe.

a6146.speaker: African Union Peace & Security Council (PSC)
a6146.speech: Raised concerns about shrinking political and civic spaces in some transitioning countries, particularly bans on political parties, associations, civil society organisations, and repression of media activities. It encouraged authorities in Burkina Faso to promote conditions conducive to political and democratic discourse, encouraging inclusivity. In Guinea, it urged authorities to pursue inclusive dialogue with all political, socio-economic, and civil society stakeholders. For Mali, it called on transitional authorities to reconsider the suspension of political parties and activities of political associations.

a6146.speaker: African Union Peace & Security Council (PSC)
a6146.speech: Reiterated its request for the AU Commission to appoint a High-Level Facilitator, preferably a current or former Head of State, to engage with transitional authorities. It also noted the leadership vacuum within the African Union Mission for Mali & the Sahel (MISAHEL), requesting the Chairperson of the AU Commission to nominate a High Representative.

a6146.speaker: African Union Peace & Security Council (PSC)
a6146.speech: Expressed concern and encouraged Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger to reconsider their decision to withdraw from ECOWAS, calling for the resumption of dialogue and mediation between ECOWAS and the three countries.

a6146.speaker: African Union Peace & Security Council (PSC)
a6146.speech: Reiterated its view on the ineligibility of transitional authority members to participate in elections, marking the end of transitions, aligning with the African Charter on Democracy, Elections & Governance.

a6303.speaker: Natangwe Ithete, Chairperson of the Standing Committee on Economics and Public Administration
a6303.speech: Has emphasised the necessity of revising and modernising the national railway system in a way that stimulates growth and development.

a6303.speaker: Iipumbu Shiimi, Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises
a6303.speech: Has requested the Nampol Inspector-General, Joseph Shikongo, to conduct a threat assessment on Namcor Board chairperson, Jennifer Comalie, and provide necessary security to her.

a6303.speaker: Marlayn Mbakera, Otjozondjupa Regional Council Chairperson
a6303.speech: Says they are hard at work to improve living conditions at Kalkfeld Settlement and move it towards Village Council status.

a6303.speaker: ||Kharas Education Forum (and its Chairperson Katrina Elizabeth |Goagoses)
a6303.speech: Has encouraged parents and the community to support learners to improve education outcomes; the Forum's Chairperson made the call on the sidelines of the annual gathering of school principals in the ||Kharas Region at Karasburg.

a6303.speaker: Moussa Faki Mahamat, Chairperson of the African Union
a6303.speech: Says Africa must create wealth amongst its people as a tool to curb foreign aid and stimulate peace ; says the need to embrace African ideas on issues facing the continent is also critical to attaining transformation across all spheres of life.

a6464.speaker: Ministry of Health statistics (Uganda)
a6464.speech: Show that about 1.3 million of Uganda’s 30 million people are infected with HIV; of these, 360,000 are eligible for Anti-retroviral Treatment (ART) because their CD4 count is below the 350 cells/mm threshold set by the World Health Organization, but only about 180,000 (50%) have access to ARVs.

a6464.speaker: Dr Watiti Stephen, AIDS activist
a6464.speech: Says that many people who are in urgent need of drugs do not get them.

a6464.speaker: Ministry of Health (Uganda) (information on PEPFAR funding)
a6464.speech: According to information from the Ministry of Health, after a long delay, PEPFAR has levelled its funding for HIV programmes, which means that many organisations will not be in position to enroll new patients on the programme while others have been allegedly closed down.

a6464.speaker: Mbabazi Rosemary, Advocacy and Public Relations Officer, Mildmay Centre
a6464.speech: Says Mildmay decided to reduce on other expenses such that money meant for treatment is not tampered with, in order to continue in operation within the means despite the overwhelming numbers ; says that all their satellite clinics countrywide continue to enroll patients on the programme.

a6464.speaker: A health practitioner who preferred anonymity
a6464.speech: Says the government prefers to keep the situation under secret to avoid causing panic among the public.

a6464.speaker: Ministry of Health (Uganda) (February press statement)
a6464.speech: Issued a press statement on the cut-off point of CD4 cell count for initiation of new AIDS patients on anti-retroviral treatment, putting it at 250 mm; the statement further read that 250 mm will be for adults and between 250 and 350 mm for infected pregnant women in case they suffer from tuberculosis, and urged all health workers at anti-retroviral centres to implement the new policy and treatment guidelines.

a6464.speaker: Dr Zainab Akol, director of the AIDS Control Programme (ACP)
a6464.speech: Says that applying the World Health Organisation standard of 350 mm means “we will have to put many people on ART, yet the funds are not available”; she adds that even then many people with such a count are healthy and refuse to take the drugs because they feel fine.

a6464.speaker: Kabakumba Masiko, Minister of Information and National Guidance
a6464.speech: While speaking to journalists at the Media Centre said there is no crisis.

a6464.speaker: Rwakimari Beatrice, Chairperson of the Parliament Standing Committee on HIV/AIDS and other related matters
a6464.speech: Says there is urgency and government needs to double its funds to cater for the increasing number of people who continue to jump on the treatment line; she adds that government needs over Shs 96 billion to support patients.

a6464.speaker: William Paton, Global Fund Director of Country Programmes
a6464.speech: Speaking at a press conference at the Media Centre, said it is logical to start with this small amount (US$4.25 million) to avoid drug shortages.

a6464.speaker: Dr Watiti Stephen and other sector experts (on financing)
a6464.speech: Say that government needs to ensure life time ART by instituting an HIV/AIDS tax.

a6547.speaker: Abia State Government
a6547.speech: Defended its decision to relocate the Umuahia campus of the Abia State University to its main campus at Uturu in Isuikwuato Local Government Area, insisting that the decision was taken in order to advance academic studies and research in the ivory tower.

a6547.speaker: Alex Otti, Governor of Abia State
a6547.speech: Speaking to reporters during his monthly media chat tagged “Governor Alex Otti Speaks to Abians” in Umuahia, said the choice is a well focused one that would give enough room for academic conviviality amongst all faculties and departments in the school; stated that the government has taken measures to address some of the challenges that may crop up as a result of the relocation exercise like accommodation, electricity, nearness to research materials and water, pointing out that challenges like nearness to internship institutions are being taken care of because his administration is currently building modern and well furnished court rooms to serve multi purposes.

a6547.speaker: Alex Otti, Governor of Abia State
a6547.speech: Said Abia State government, in partnership with the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), will soon begin the renovation of major water projects in Abia, adding that the agreement will begin with the rehabilitation of Ariaria, Abia North and Ubakala, Umuahia South water schemes.

a6547.speaker: Alex Otti, Governor of Abia State
a6547.speech: On why Southeast governors have continued to maintain apathy on the clamour to release Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, leader of the Indigenous Peoples of Biafra (IPOB), stated that he does not believe in unnecessary showmanship and media blitz to impress some quarters, adding that he has on some occasions personally taken the matter of the release of the IPOB leader to the President: “I have personally being engaging the relevant authorities on his release. I want him to come out. I don’t believe in media show. I have gone to the President to talk about his release; it’s not what we’ll discuss in the media space.”

a6547.speaker: Alex Otti, Governor of Abia State
a6547.speech: On why his party, the Labour Party, lost woefully in the just concluded Local Government Elections conducted by ABSIEC, insisted that he is still a member of LP and attributed the party’s loss to the relatively unknown Zenith Labour Party to internal squabbles in LP: “I can assure you that I’m still in LP. The crisis in LP made our supporters to go elsewhere. They know those that would deliver. I believe that that was what happened in this case right from the time I stood up to contest the election in 2015. When I left PDP to join APGA, our people followed me and I won that election even when APGA has not won even one councillorship before that time. We took half of the House of Assembly in 2015. So, sometimes, people recognize the fact that political parties are empty platforms to contest and win elections and when you muddle up things in your political parties, you give advantage, create opportunities for your competitors and that was what happened in the last LG election. I authorized my followers to join any political party that they liked and majority of them moved into other political parties. However, I remain in the Labour Party.”

a6560.speaker: India's Press Information Bureau
a6560.speech: Reported the ceremony was attended by the High Commissioner of India in Mozambique, Robert Shetkintong, India's newly appointed Defence Adviser at Maputo, Colonel Puneet Attri, and the Commanding Officer of INS Gharial, Commander Rajan Chib.

a6560.speaker: Indian government
a6560.speech: Said the two vessels will significantly aid the Government of Mozambique in its effort to combat maritime terrorism and ongoing insurgency in the Cabo Delgado province ; Added that the interceptor vessels gifted by India have played a pivotal role since 2019 in anti-insurgency operations, maritime patrol and interdiction, and logistics support missions ; "The Indian Navy has been collaborating with several friendly littorals of the Indian Ocean Region to equip and train their maritime security forces to counter maritime security challenges like piracy, drug and human trafficking, Illegal Unreported and Unregulated (IUU) fishing, maritime terrorism, etc. The Indian Navy has also been the first responder to provide Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) support to several nations in the region during natural calamities and other contingencies like the COVID-19 pandemic" ; "India and Mozambique share a robust strategic partnership that has grown even stronger with each passing year in multiple realms. India is thus fully committed to helping and supporting its maritime neighbours in the Indian Ocean Region in line with the vision of Security and Growth for all in the region (SAGAR) advocated by the Honorable Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi."

a6560.speaker: SpokespersonNavy (@indiannavy), Indian Navy spokesperson, post on X, November 9, 2024
a6560.speech: "#INSGharial arrives at Nacala Port, Mozambique! Towards fostering & strengthening #maritimesecurity in the region & building #BridgesofFriendship, the #IndianNavy handed over two Fast Interceptor Crafts to the #MozambicanArmedForces. A significant moment for the GoI's Vision of…"

a6560.speaker: India in Mozambique (@IndiainMoz), post on X, November 11, 2024
a6560.speech: "India gifted two Fast Interceptor Crafts (8 Nov 2024) to Mozambique Navy at a formal ceremony in Nacala in northern. High Commissioner Robert Shetkintong and Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of National Defence Mr Augusto Casimiro Mueio attended the event. #IndiaMozambique"

a6560.speaker: High Commission of India in Mozambique
a6560.speech: Said the first edition of the India-Mozambique Defence Industrial Interaction gave an opportunity for government and private defence companies from India to come together with officials from the Ministries of Defence, Mozambican military (FADM) and Mozambican civil security agencies to discuss cooperation in defence production and procurement.

a6764.speaker: Dileita Mohamed Dileita, President of Djibouti's National Assembly
a6764.speech: Thanked the director general of the Emirati Red Crescent centre for his generosity and expressed his wish for the strengthening of cooperation.

a6897.speaker: Constantino Andre, Secretary-General of the OJM (Mozambican Youth Organization)
a6897.speech: Encourages Televisao de Mocambique to strengthen its promotion of Mozambican youth; hopes to see young people's concerns reflected in the public broadcaster's content, but also the youth effort for the country's development.

a6897.speaker: Decentralized governance bodies in Inhambane
a6897.speech: Demand that the Local Development Agreements implemented by SASOL be aligned with the province's development plans. The concern was raised at the first meeting evaluating projects implemented under the ADL in the districts of Govuro, Inhassoro and Vilankulo.

a6897.speaker: Salim Vala, Minister of Planning and Development
a6897.speech: Says that cooperation with European businesspeople is fundamental to the country's economic development. He was speaking this Monday in Maputo during a meeting with Mozambican businesspeople and representatives of the chambers of commerce of European Union countries.

a6897.speaker: Daniel Chapo, commander-in-chief of the Defence and Security Forces / President of the Republic
a6897.speech: Wants an increasingly modernized Mozambican Navy, republican, committed to peace and valuing human resources. This was one of several demands made during the swearing-in of the new commander of the Navy and the commissioning of various officers.

a6897.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic
a6897.speech: Says the commissioning of senior officers of the Defence and Security Forces represents recognition of merit, dedication and service rendered to the Mozambican State, above all in the struggle for sovereignty and the guarantee of public order and tranquillity.

a6897.speaker: Livestock sector (Gaza province)
a6897.speech: According to the livestock sector, in that part of the country the loss of the animals directly or indirectly affects more than 17,000 herders.

a6897.speaker: Agricultural authorities in Manica
a6897.speech: Guarantee that they have brought under control the fruit fly pest that has plagued the province for roughly ten years.

a6973.speaker: European Parliament / MEPs (statement)
a6973.speech: Say in a statement that with the 2025 EU budget they managed to "restore the Council's cuts, strengthen the main EU programmes and manage borrowing costs" ; the European assembly stresses that "the 2025 budget will be 6% higher than this year's, which means an increase of 10 billion euros," speaking of "more effective support to confront challenges such as health, humanitarian aid, border management and climate action" ; according to the European Parliament, "more than 230 million euros added for key programmes aimed at improving people's lives, increasing competitiveness and tackling current challenges" are also foreseen.

a6973.speaker: European Commission
a6973.speech: Had proposed last July a 2025 budget that included 199.7 billion euros in commitments, equivalent to 1.08% of the EU's gross national income, and 152.7 billion euros in payments.

a6973.speaker: European Court of Auditors
a6973.speech: Said last October that there are "ever-increasing" risks to the European Union's budget, because of record debt, Russia's war against Ukraine and high inflation.

a7024.speaker: Hage Geingob, President of Namibia
a7024.speech: Says that the administering of tax laws and collection of state revenue demand high standards of integrity and customer-centric service delivery, which should permeate in the day-to-day operations of Namibia Revenue Agency (NamRA) ; “The public expects NamRA to be an exemplary institution that will foster a fine balance between economic growth and trade functions as well as providing tax services to all taxpayers.”

a7024.speaker: Madhuri (cited author on tax reform)
a7024.speech: Asserted that, “Tax reform is a policy implementation by the government through which few alterations are made into the tax system in order to overcome the loopholes and enhance the effectiveness of the tax administration in the country in order to generate higher revenues from taxes as compared to the overall spending”.

a7024.speaker: Namibia Revenue Agency (NamRA)
a7024.speech: The agency suggests that more emphasis should be put on revenue enhancement through policy and administration reforms; according to its website, NamRA employed people with a wealth of experience.

a7109.speaker: John Kapito, Consumers Association of Malawi Executive Director
a7109.speech: Faulted banks for the tariff increases, rating it as a "rip-off" for consumers: "It is a challenging time for consumers, especially as we are encouraged to adopt digital banking. Yet, financial institutions seem to be taking advantage by imposing higher charges each year."

a7109.speaker: Lyness Nkungula, Bankers Association of Malawi Chief Executive Officer
a7109.speech: Said the tariff hikes are a response to the current economic climate and a necessary step to enhance bank operations: "Operational costs have risen significantly, largely due to the increased reliance on technology, which requires constant upgrades. With inflation impacting various aspects of the business, it's essential for banks to adjust fees accordingly."

a7168.speaker: Memo reviewed by Reuters
a7168.speech: According to the memo, the decision affects countries supported by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), sparking concerns of a global health crisis.

a7168.speaker: USAID source and a former agency official (anonymous)
a7168.speech: Said the memo sent to Chemonics directs the firm to halt operations related to HIV, malaria, tuberculosis, contraception, and maternal and child health supplies.

a7168.speaker: Atul Gawande, former global health chief at USAID
a7168.speech: “This is catastrophic,” said Atul Gawande. “Donated drug supplies keeping 20 million people with HIV alive stop today.” ; Warned that treatment interruptions could lead to disease resurgence, drug resistance, and increased transmission of HIV.

a7168.speaker: Sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a7168.speech: Said the freeze affects organizations supporting 6.5 million orphans and vulnerable children with HIV in 23 countries, prevents medicine deliveries to clinics and could shutter clinics funded by U.S. assistance.

a7168.speaker: Experts and advocates
a7168.speech: Warn the aid freeze could have devastating consequences for millions relying on these programs.

a7168.speaker: USAID and Chemonics
a7168.speech: Have not yet responded to requests for comment.

a7168.speaker: USAID website
a7168.speech: On its website, USAID says it supports HIV prevention, care, and treatment in over 50 countries including Nigeria, Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burma, Burundi, Cambodia, Cameroon, Nepal and Nicaragua.

a7183.speaker: Ben Turney, Kavango Resources Plc chief executive officer
a7183.speech: “As the prices of gold and copper continue to rise, this is an ideal time to make major discoveries in both metals” ; “We will use some of the funds raised in the bookbuild to take the diamond drill rig back to Hillside to test the strike, width, and extent of these possible discoveries.” ; “We are keen to start this landmark drill campaign and will use some of the funds raised to deploy a second rig to the Karakubis Project. This will halve the time it takes for us to complete the programme.”

a7183.speaker: Initial assay results from Kavango Resources' Hillside Prospect 4 gold project in Zimbabwe
a7183.speech: suggest the potential for over one million ounces of mineable gold.

a7200.speaker: Humanitarian organisations
a7200.speech: Say the conflict in the country's North Kivu province is hindering their work to contain mpox.

a7200.speaker: Samuel Roger Kamba Mulamba, DRC Health Minister
a7200.speech: In a televised press briefing, explained the context and history around the mpox outbreak: "Smallpox was eradicated by the vaccine, finished! In the early 1970s, 1980s and late 1990s there were still people vaccinated against smallpox." ; "So, when mpox had an outbreak they were still protected by the same vaccine." ; "The problem is that there are fewer people born before 1980, which means young people are not protected by the old vaccination." ; "This explains that people are not protected from being contaminated."

a7200.speaker: Samuel Roger Kamba Mulamba, DRC Health Minister
a7200.speech: Said Belgium was set to supply 215 000 vaccines, while Japan, one of the major mpox vaccine manufacturers through KM Biologics, pledged three million doses ; "We will have vaccines arriving next week," he said in French, addressing journalists in a televised conference in Kinshasa.

a7200.speaker: UNICEF
a7200.speech: Has requested almost R85.5 million to expand its operations in the country, and requires a further R19 million for regional preparedness, coordination and response efforts.

a7200.speaker: Jambo Lab (web-based platform for humanitarian work in the DRC)
a7200.speech: "Members of local communities subscribe to our digital platform and receive SMS alerts in the local language with essential information on mpox and preventive measures to reduce the risks of contamination," the organisation said.

a7200.speaker: USAID (US donor arm)
a7200.speech: Has not said how many vaccines will come through.

a7200.speaker: Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance
a7200.speech: Also promised to make vaccines available to all countries affected globally through a R9.5 billion fund.

a7200.speaker: Hayley MacGregor, research fellow at the Institute of Development Studies in the UK
a7200.speech: Added the outbreak in the DRC was a "sober example of the challenges to humanitarian responses during conflict, insecurity, displacement, and poor access to healthcare".

a7200.speaker: Heather Kerr, International Rescue Committee (IRC) country director in the DRC
a7200.speech: "Humanitarian actors are struggling to control the outbreak due to insufficient resources." ; "Currently, many displaced persons and communities in Goma, who are already struggling without necessities, are exposed to high risks of disease, with children and young people being particularly vulnerable." ; "The international community must seize the opportunity presented by the recent humanitarian truce and ceasefire signed on July 30 in Luanda, Angola, to act swiftly."

a7200.speaker: Heather Kerr, International Rescue Committee (IRC) country director in the DRC
a7200.speech: "The IRC is preparing to launch a response against mpox in North Kivu province, specifically targeting the internally displaced person camps of Bulengo, Rusayo2, and Nzulo, located around the city of Goma." ; "The overcrowding, lack of hygiene facilities and basic infrastructure expose this population to a high risk of the epidemic spreading."

a7223.speaker: Moses Moloi, Board Member of Farmers United
a7223.speech: Has said that horticulture farmers lose over 65 percent of their produce due to lack of value chains upstream and downstream. “Our produce is rotting because we don’t have processing facilities that will prevent produce from being wasted,” Moloi said, adding that the youth of the country should take advantage of this market gap and create an additional value chain ; He emphasised the need for value chain in the horticulture industry to promote growth and satisfy the national demand ; “As a nation we don’t have proper collaboration of farmers, we work as individuals and this compromises sustainable growth of the industry,” Moloi said.

a7223.speaker: Moses Moloi, Board Member of Farmers United
a7223.speech: Stated that one of the major problems affecting the horticulture industry is retail shops sabotage. “The retail shops are saying there is shortage of supply but this is not true because they don’t buy all our produce. What happens is that they place orders of certain quantities but upon delivery they reduce the amount then we will be forced to return with those products and we end up selling at a loss.”

a7223.speaker: Moses Moloi, Board Member of Farmers United
a7223.speech: He said government needs to set up policies that guide farmers, as well as address competition issues. “We need to get to a point where we set up policies that support the bona-fide Motswana so that we can protect our farmers. Government must understand how policy shifts encourage competition.”

a7223.speaker: Thabo Thamane, Chief Executive Officer of the Citizen Entrepreneurial Development Agency (CEDA)
a7223.speech: Responding to questions from the participants during the FNBB national Budget Review, Thabo Thamane said the horticulture business industry is affected by man-made dynamics which are deliberately created by large retailers. “The issue of low supply which is coming from large retailers is not true. We are currently experiencing trade wars that are deliberately created so that small scale producers will not be able to grow.”

a7223.speaker: Mohamed Osman, Sefalana Group Finance Director
a7223.speech: Said they experienced a shortage of fruits and vegetables on an intermittent basis for some time now. “With borders closed, we are dependent on local farmers being able to produce appropriate quantities of produce at the right quality. This varies from farmer to farmer, so there are times where there simply is not enough to fulfil the market’s demand. In the past, the shortfall would be imported.” ; He said Sefalana buys both grain and fresh produce from about 800 local farmers ; “Retailers are supporting more and more farmers all the time. If quality is not at the right level however, retailers will not be comfortable with putting their produce on the shelves. This is normal supply and demand. Customers will not demand produce at below acceptable standards.”

a7239.speaker: Brazilian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a7239.speech: Said on Wednesday that it was in the "final stages" of submitting a formal intervention to the ICJ regarding the case, originally brought by South Africa: "The international community cannot remain inactive in the face of ongoing atrocities" ; "Brazil believes there is no longer room for moral ambiguity or political omission. Impunity undermines international legality and undermines the credibility of the multilateral system." ; the "Brazilian government announces that it is in the final stages of submitting a formal intervention in the ongoing case at the International Court of Justice, brought by South Africa under the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide" ; "The Brazilian government expresses deep indignation at the recurring episodes of violence against the civilian population in the State of Palestine, not limited to the Gaza Strip but extending to the West Bank." ; said that civilians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank have been subjected to "recurring episodes of violence" and serious rights violations, including the "shameless use of starvation as a weapon of war" ; noted that the decision to intervene in the case is based on the "plausibility that the rights of Palestinians to protection against acts of genocide are being irreversibly impaired".

a7239.speaker: Folha de S Paulo (Brazilian newspaper)
a7239.speech: Earlier reported Brazil's planned intervention in the case.

a7239.speaker: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, President of Brazil
a7239.speech: Denounced Israel's actions in Gaza as a genocide at a BRICS meeting earlier this month.

a7239.speaker: Israeli Embassy in Brasilia
a7239.speech: Said the Brazilian statement used "harsh words that do not fully portray the reality of what is currently happening in Gaza", while Brazil had also "completely ignored" the role of Hamas.

a7239.speaker: CONIB, Brazil's National Israeli association (statement)
a7239.speech: Said in a statement in response to Wednesday's decision: "The breaking of Brazil's longstanding friendship and partnership with Israel is a misguided move that proves the extremism of our foreign policy."

a7239.speaker: International Court of Justice (ICJ) order, January 2024
a7239.speech: Issued an order in January 2024, demanding that Israel take action to prevent genocide in the Strip through acts such as allowing greater access to humanitarian aid.

a7239.speaker: United Nations officials
a7239.speech: Have denounced the GHF distribution sites as "death traps", and said they will not cooperate with the GHF, which supplanted existing international aid groups that Israel has largely barred from operating in Gaza.

a7404.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a7404.speech: Announced on Friday night that Rasool had been declared persona non grata, accusing him of being a “race-baiting politician” who harbours hostility toward America and President Donald Trump; stated on social media platform X: “South Africa's Ambassador to the United States is no longer welcome in our great country” ; “We have nothing to discuss with him and so he is considered PERSONA NON GRATA.”

a7404.speaker: Trump administration
a7404.speech: Cited South Africa's land reform policies, which it claims unfairly target white farmers, as the reason for the aid suspension.

a7404.speaker: South Africa (government)
a7404.speech: Has denied these allegations, asserting that the reforms aim to address historical inequalities.

a7404.speaker: South African Presidency (statement)
a7404.speech: Responded to the expulsion on Saturday, calling it “regrettable” and urging all parties to maintain diplomatic decorum: “South Africa remains committed to building a mutually beneficial relationship with the United States of America.”
